title: Swap two elements of the caller's array

blocks.text: A method cannot swap two `int` variables of its caller: it receives copies of their values. It can swap two elements of an array, because it receives a copy of the reference to the caller's own array, and both references point to the same elements. Assigning a new array to the parameter, on the other hand, only changes the method's copy:
Write `swap(int[] values, int i, int j)` in `Swapper`. It swaps `values[i]` and `values[j]` in the caller's array and returns nothing:

items: swapping an element with itself changes nothing: `swap(values, 1, 1)` keeps `{3, 2, 1}`.

cases.says: swap(values, 1, 1) keeps the element: the XOR trick would zero it.

concepts: A method that changes the elements of an array it was passed changes the caller's array, since both references point to it.
